_purpose: The CONTRADICTION TEST (Amendment 16). If 14-15 of the 16 NAMED elements already arrive unprompted, 'did the element land' has a denominator of one and cannot separate 'the specification works' from 'the LoRA, mesh and control already produce this dwarf'. So: name elements that CONFLICT with what arrives unbidden, and measure whether the prompt overrides the supplied attribute. Prompt wins -> identity is in the prompt and the route generalises. Supplied attribute wins -> the pipeline produces this dwarf in different clothes.
_baseline: E08-spec-prompt.json (the SPEC arm). This file is that prompt with the contradicted attributes SUBSTITUTED IN PLACE. Phrase count, phrase order, phrase structure and every other word are identical, so prompt length and term count are pinned and the substituted adjectives are the only variable. Same input render, same exact-silhouette mask, same control image, same seed 770700, same sampler settings.
_denominator: EIGHT elements are contradicted and COUNTED: N2 beard red->white, N3 tunic green->blue, N4 pauldrons gold->silver, N6 belt medallion gold->silver, N8 skirt dark red->black, N12 knee plates gold->silver, N15 crossguard gold->silver, N16 pommel gold->silver.
_not_counted: N5 scrollwork, N9 skirt panels and N11 forearm plate are ALSO substituted gold->silver / green->grey, for prompt coherence only. They are the three declared co-location cases with a pre-registered prediction of their own (Amendment 15) and are reported SEPARATELY, outside the denominator. Mixing them in would confound the contradiction question with the co-location question.
_held: N1 bald head, N7 brown leather belt, N10 brown leather bracers, N13 heavy dark boots, N14 massive greatsword are NOT contradicted. They are internal controls: if they move as much as the contradicted elements, the image repainted globally and per-element attribution is weak.
